items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: Then I went with Stuff Smith. ... I'd been in with Stuff Smith in Chicago

ctx.x: Yeah. Then after a week or so, they realized that we were a pretty good band but they had already booked Charlie Barnet to follow us, so that was the end of our 52nd Street career. But then, by the same token, John Kirby just opened at the Onyx Club, Stuff Smith. Stuff Smith had opened the Onyx Club and then, John Kirby. This is pre-war, World War II.
But up until then you were above

items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: I loved playing with him. ... I remember Stuff had the band with Cozy and Jonah, and John Brown was on bass... And they were at the Green Room at the Edison Hotel.

ctx.x: -- gorgeous, gorgeous. I loved playing with him. He -- I called him a pixie. He had a ball wherever he was, whenever, however. I remember Stuff had the band with Cozy and Jonah, and John Brown was on bass, and I forget who the piano player was at the time. And they were at the Green Room at the Edison Hotel.

And Stuff saw a chick pass that had a pretty voluptuous bottom, and he remarked about it. And somebody said, 'I dare you to touch it.' And he touched it with the bow. The band got fired if he didn't leave.
